questions.question_text:
A personal loan of $\$18\,000$ charges $9\%$ p.a. compounded monthly with monthly repayments of $\$420$.
Which recurrence relation models the loan balance $A_{n}$ after $n$ months?

options.why: Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.
Added repayments instead of subtracting them from the loan balance.
Multiplied by the interest rate alone instead of the growth factor $1+r$.

questions.question_text:
A debt of $\$6000$ has a monthly interest rate of $1\%$ ($r=0.01$) and monthly repayments of $\$250$.
Which expression represents the balance $A_{2}$ after $2$ repayments?

options.why: Subtracted simple total repayments without compounding the first repayment.
Applied an extra power of the growth factor to the first repayment.
Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$7200$ charges $8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly. Repayments of $\$450$ are made at the end of each quarter.
Which expression gives the balance $A_{3}$ after the third repayment?

options.why: Used the annual rate instead of dividing it by $4$ for quarterly periods.
Subtracted three repayments without compounding the earlier repayments.
Added the repayment series instead of subtracting it from the loan balance.

questions.question_text:
A car loan of $\$22\,000$ incurs interest at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) with monthly repayments of $\$500$.
Which is the correct expanded expression for $A_{3}$?

options.why: Compounded the first two repayments for $3$ and $2$ periods instead of $2$ and $1$ periods; there are still three repayment terms.
Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.
Treated repayments as a simple uncompounded lump sum.

questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$14\,000$ charges interest at $7.8\%$ p.a. compounded half-yearly with half-yearly repayments of $\$1200$.
What is the recurrence relation for the balance $A_{n}$?

options.why: Used the annual rate for half-yearly periods.
Added the repayments instead of subtracting them from the debt.
Divided the annual rate by 12 instead of 2 for half-yearly compounding.

questions.question_text:
A borrower takes a loan of $\$40\,000$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) and makes monthly repayments of $\$180$.
What will happen to the loan balance $A_{n}$ over time?

options.text: The balance increases each month because the monthly repayment of $\$180$ is less than the first month's interest of $\$200$.
The balance decreases steadily to zero after approximately $222$ months.
options.why: Assumed repayments always pay off the loan regardless of the interest amount.

options.text: The balance remains constant at $\$40\,000$ every month.
options.why: Assumed the repayment exactly balances the monthly interest charge.

options.text: The loan is paid off in fewer than $100$ months due to compounding.
options.why: Mistakenly believed compounding accelerates loan payoff even when repayments are below interest.

questions.solution_text:
First month interest $=40\,000\times0.005=\$200$
$A_{1}=40\,000(1.005)-180=40\,200-180=\$40\,020$
Since the repayment is less than the interest added, the balance increases indefinitely.

questions.question_text:
A mortgage of $\$360\,000$ charges $6.3\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, with repayments of $\$2400$ at the end of each month.
Which series expression gives the balance $A_{n}$ after $n$ repayments while the debt remains outstanding?

options.why: Used the annual rate for monthly repayment periods.
Subtracted the total repayments without compounding the earlier repayments.
Compounded every repayment for one extra period, as though repayments were made at the beginning of each month.
